narrative.overview: Oneinfo bridges durable, precision-engineered hardware with warm, modern editorial craft. Inspired by matte architectural paper, deep forest inks, and the tactile snap of physical business cards, the visual language balances grounded substance with electric digital immediacy. The surfaces avoid generic corporate SaaS sterility; instead, they evoke a workshop of considered materials where every printed millimeter and encoded byte is deliberate.
keyCharacteristics: Material Grounding: Warm paper backgrounds and deep forest inks anchor the experience in physical reality.
Electric Telemetry: Vibrant acid lime and mint serve as high-visibility signal lights for NFC taps and primary actions.
Tactile Weight: Generous card corner radii, solid pill action triggers, and deep ambient drop shadows communicate tangible physical objects.
Disciplined Precision: Hairline translucent dividers and uppercase tracked labels establish industrial clarity.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Electric Lime (#b9f56a) must never cover more than 5% of any view. Its authority comes entirely from contrast against deep ink and neutral paper.

rules.name: The Surface Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Dark ink cards float over warm paper, never over deep dark backgrounds without a hairline separation border.

rules.name: The No-Float Headings Rule
rules.body: Headings must never sit isolated above content with equal margin above and below; they anchor closely to following copy.

rules.name: The Resting Flat Rule
rules.body: Functional data tables, form inputs, and status badges remain strictly flat at rest. Shadows are reserved for physical cards and floating triggers.

dos: Do anchor layouts around physical card representations and tactile finishes.
Do use Electric Lime (#b9f56a) strictly as an intentional signal for active NFC states, confirmation dots, and primary CTAs.
Do maintain the canonical 1.585 aspect ratio whenever depicting Oneinfo smart cards.
Do pair bold high-contrast display headlines with generously tracked uppercase micro-labels.
Do preserve the tactile paper canvas (#fbfaf5) on public storefront views.
donts: Don't use generic vibrant purple/blue gradient fills; stick to rich natural emerald/forest gradients or deep carbon tones.
Don't apply heavy drop shadows to flat administrative tables and data lists.
Don't shrink body copy below 14px on mobile profiles or checkout forms.
Don't crowd touch targets; buttons and interactive card chips must maintain a minimum touch area of 44x44px.
Don't rely on color alone for hardware pass/fail verification; always pair color with clear iconographic and textual status cues.
